title: SPC watch probabilities for 13,003 US watches in 2006-2025 did not increase enough with watch area and duration; hail-count and 65-kt wind errors followed rule and practice changes
abstract:
We verified the seven probabilities that the NOAA Storm Prediction Center (SPC) issues with each tornado and severe thunderstorm watch. The sample was 13,003 watches from 2006 to 2025. The outcomes were reports in the SPC final storm databases. The analysis plan was written before reports were matched to watches.

Five of seven probabilities were miscalibrated by the pre-set rule (95% CI of observed/forecast O/F excludes 1 and error above 10%): at least 10 severe hail reports (O/F 0.65), at least one EF2+ tornado (0.78), at least 2 tornadoes (0.85), at least 10 wind reports (0.86) and at least one wind of 65 kt or more (1.36, too low). Hail of 2 in or more (0.98) and 6 combined reports (0.94) were within the margin.

The largest systematic error is watch size. At a fixed issued probability, the event chance increased with watch area x duration for all seven events. The forecasts carry only 26-53% of this dependence: O/F is 0.26-0.93 in the smallest fifth of watches and 0.94-1.71 in the largest fifth. A recalibration with log(area x hours), fitted on 2006-2015, reduced the 2016-2025 Brier score by 1.4-5.1% against a plain recalibration for all seven events. County-based watch areas with actual clearing times gave the same results (O/F within 0.04).

Exploratory checks: the 10-hail-report over-forecast increased when the severe hail size changed from 0.75 to 1.00 in (2010) and the forecasts did not follow; counted at 0.75 in, the 2010-2025 O/F returns to the pre-2010 value. The 65-kt wind error comes from low forecasts in 2013-2017 (O/F 2.16) and from more measured gusts after 2018. In tornado watches, the 2-tornado probability was calibrated; in severe thunderstorm watches it was too high (O/F 0.66).

Limitations: storm reports are incomplete and depend on population and practice; the verification area of the probabilities is not stated by SPC; the source checks after the plan are exploratory.
